text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Cardiology consultation in two weeks with coronary CT angiography for suspected stable angina, and advice on revascularization and on fitness for the expedition
  • Medical therapy from intake for suspected angina: aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, metoprolol succinate, and sublingual nitroglycerin with written instructions to call emergency services if pain lasts more than 5 minutes after the first dose
  • Stop smoking: varenicline for 12 weeks, with the option of 12 more, a quit date in one week, counseling at each visit, and the quitline
  • AUDIT with a brief intervention for hazardous drinking: no more than two drinks a day and several alcohol-free days a week, with AUDIT-C at follow-up
  • Prediabetes: diet and activity counseling and HbA1c in about four months
  • Raise metoprolol succinate to 100 mg for persisting angina, with an echocardiogram, and revascularization of the proximal LAD lesion if angina persists despite medical therapy or he prefers it after a shared decision
  • Expedition plan: a symptom-limited exercise test before departure, a written cardiac summary with ECG and stent card, three months' extra medicines split between two bags, an automated external defibrillator and emergency cardiac medicines on board, a satellite link for telemedicine, an evacuation plan to the nearest cardiac centers along the route, and advice on cold stress
  • Invasive coronary angiography with a drug-eluting stent to the proximal LAD, then aspirin with clopidogrel for six months and aspirin alone after
  • Cardiac rehabilitation after the stent, three sessions a week until departure, with a home exercise plan for the voyage
  • Add ezetimibe 10 mg because LDL cholesterol was 62 mg/dL on atorvastatin 80 mg, above the target below 55

resource.title: Ernest Shackleton synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care and cardiology for a 47-year-old expedition leader and heavy smoker with new exertional chest tightness and breathlessness, four months before leading a ship-based polar expedition: pretest probability and risk assessment, a resting ECG and risk-factor tests, coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR as the first test, an echocardiogram, guideline-directed medical therapy (aspirin, high-intensity statin with ezetimibe to an LDL below 55 mg/dL, a beta-blocker, and sublingual nitroglycerin), revascularization when angina persists despite medical therapy and what it does and does not offer in chronic coronary disease, dual antiplatelet therapy, cardiac rehabilitation, varenicline with counseling, the AUDIT with a brief intervention, prediabetes, and fitness for remote high-latitude travel: a symptom-limited exercise test, an evacuation plan, a defibrillator and medicines on board, and cold stress. His reluctance to be examined, and to let anything stop the expedition, is worked through with shared decision-making. Built on the 1918 AHA/ACC chronic coronary disease guideline, the 1919 ESC chronic coronary syndromes guideline, and the CMID ischemic heart disease and hyperlipidemia monographs.
